validation: Public-Python returns and all fully defined MAIN columns, standard subtables and owning references compare against CASA before alternating timings. No skipped comparison. The 73-case oracle separately covers read-only big-endian input and both stale-control-count cases.
interpretation: Contiguous payload/shape borrowing, pending-column reuse, sorted sparse lookup and adjacent output-bucket batching preserve all scientific outputs. Controlled native 300k full medians improve 0.364→0.274 s, with write phase 0.213→0.125 s; user/system CPU falls. Output MAIN 60k calls fall from 1,882 reads/3,757 seeks/1,875 writes to 83/159/76. Public-Python 60k full is 0.099–0.120 s versus CASA 5.190–5.616 s; 300k full is 0.539–0.603 s versus 27.113–27.436 s. Current warm CPU/wall remains near one and cold remains materially CPU-active. This is not an I/O-limited acceptance pass; #990 stays open until remaining CPU cost is corrected or the owner explicitly accepts a measured fluxscale-specific tradeoff under #979. Exact regenerated public input has the same row counts/shapes/file sizes as the retained diagnostic and no new read/seek storm; no broader writer/decoder redesign has been started. Existing table-reader/rewrite references are older software baselines, not raw-disk floors.
storage_tradeoff: Appending replacement records preserves shared old records and the source storage layout. The measured full native product is 11,588,220 bytes versus 10,632,989 bytes from CASA (about 9% larger); obsolete payloads remain unreferenced. Unsupported storage layouts and incomplete copied row counts use the validated reconstruction path.

diagnostic_callgrind_scope: Current candidate on 60,000-row gains with fixed HISTORY. Total 370,979,779 versus 403,025,939 before this correction; full_output::save inclusive 135,900,704 (36.6%), sparse saver 46,081,778 (12.4%), estimator 45,995,829 (12.4%). Inclusive costs overlap. Costs are distributed among canonical table decoding/encoding, generic cell ownership, metadata and arithmetic.
